scope: Add a digest-pinned PostgreSQL 16 GitHub Actions service and disposable uniquely named databases for reward quality tests
Exercise repository migrations from zero and through concurrent initialization
Exercise two-connection final-budget, same-wallet, claim-idempotency, reservation expiry and cancellation, UTC rollover, and payout-lease authority
Exercise durable restart and reconciliation from in-progress, queued, signed, ambiguous broadcast, inclusion, and finality boundaries without constructing a second logical transaction
Run one built Chromium Daily journey against the real PostgreSQL store in record-only mode and verify durable rows afterward
Add deterministic fake payout fault coverage for balance, fee, signer, network, stale head, outage, invalid response, delayed inclusion, finality, expiry, exact-byte rebroadcast, and manual review
Add quality-test startup guards, production security-header assertions, and reward secret/server-dependency artifact scans
Integrate focused scripts, CI routing, documentation, and compact completion evidence
non_goals: A real Nimiq Pay provider, real wallet, recovery words, private payout key, Render database, external RPC, public chain, or NIM transfer
Testnet or mainnet reward mode in any autonomous process
Horizontal scaling, durable active simulations, PvP, matchmaking, automatic replacement of ambiguous payouts, or multiple concurrent signers
Bundle and timing budgets, verify:full closure, or workflow-wide performance partitioning assigned to WP-014E
Production art, audio, Nimiq brand assets, or Sorcerers code or assets

13 tests passed, including PostgreSQL browser authority refusal and reward artifact scan fixtures.
23 tests passed, including quality-mode authority guards, payout preparation faults, delayed finality, expiry, exact-byte reuse, and security headers.
The maintained Chromium and WebKit Daily routes passed; three reviewed project exclusions remained.
The Mini App SDK remains lazy in the client and @nimiq/core remains server-only outside centralized test support.
No payout-key fixture, wallet proof, session token, or server-only marker leaked into inspected source, build, or generated text artifacts.
Compliance, types, server, and client production builds passed; the existing client chunk warning remains assigned to WP-014E.
Built server, overlays, approved-asset plumbing, and join-ID API passed.
All 150 local Windows logic results passed with one worker and zero retries: 94 passed and 56 reviewed exclusions in 5.5 minutes. Linux screenshot comparison remains CI-only.

check_results.command: PostgreSQL image digest and safety-boundary review
check_results.detail: The official Docker Hub tag metadata was checked for postgres:16.10-bookworm and CI pins its multi-architecture digest sha256:38471f330eb885e04de130b768d6db4e10469e2311879c7e5c699f6d2d8a1c74. Test startup and runners reject chain modes, payout authority, repeat-attempt overrides, external databases, and unsafe database names.
Compliance and reward-security scans pass. The slice adds no dependency or asset, uses one centralized synthetic key fixture, adds no client payout authority, and does not use Sorcerers material.

Reviewed serialized migrations, two-pool contention, claim idempotency, advisory signer lease, restart boundaries, exact signed-byte reuse, browser ledger assertions, database cleanup, zero retries, CI time bounds, and generated-artifact retention. No production reward policy or external authority was enabled.

skipped_checks: npm run test:reward:postgres and npm run test:browser:reward:postgres were not run locally because this Windows environment has neither Docker nor psql; the digest-pinned Ubuntu PostgreSQL job is mandatory before completion.
Physical Android/iOS and Nimiq Pay WebView testing was not run; browser automation and synthetic wallet providers do not substitute for it.
residual_risks: The new PostgreSQL migrations, races, restart boundaries, and built-browser durable journey are type/discovery checked locally but require their first authoritative disposable-service CI execution.
Sessions and active simulations remain single-process and non-durable; WP-014D hardens reward liabilities but does not add horizontal runtime authority.
